plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question asks only which hallmark pathways change between the treated (psoriasis lesional) and control skin samples. Differential expression is already done and delivered as /data/inputs/results/de_results.csv (12,000 genes x 8 columns: gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2_fold_change_se, stat, p_value, p_adj-style columns from a DESeq2 treated-vs-control contrast), so no new model is fitted — planning a fresh DE run would be unasked scope and would risk a contrast that disagrees with the delivered table.

The plan therefore has two working steps plus a report. First, a sample-structure check on the delivered counts (counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 12 samples + gene id column; metadata.csv, 12 samples x 2 columns with condition) — the profile flags that sample_01 has a library size roughly 4x below the median, and that sample must be inspected on the PCA and the sample-distance heatmap rather than silently dropped. This step does not refit anything; it establishes whether the delivered DE table rests on samples that group by condition, and whether sample_01 sits apart. It is a sanity anchor on the inherited result, not a gate.

Second, preranked GSEA (fgsea) over the FULL ranked list of all tested genes in de_results.csv against the MSigDB human hallmark collection (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols, staged as the 2026.1 human release). The ranking metric is the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the `stat` column) — a stated choice on a disputed point: it is signed and scaled by its standard error, so it neither inflates low-count genes the way an unshrunken log2 fold change does nor produces the rank ties a signed p-value produces when p-values saturate. The list is not thresholded before the test. The contrast direction is fixed by the delivered table: positive stat = higher in treated (psoriasis lesional) than control; the step must verify and state this against the metadata reference level. Set size window 15–500 after intersecting with the tested genes, BH adjustment, fixed seed, redundant leading-edge-overlapping sets collapsed.

The hallmark collection is present in the reference store for human, so the central question is answerable. GO BP/CC/MF and the oncogenic C6 collection are also staged and are named as an optional secondary pass in the same step only if hallmark results warrant a mechanism-level follow-up; Reactome and WikiPathways-human are available too but hallmark alone answers the question as asked, so the secondary collections are annotation, not the deliverable. The report states database and version, rank metric, universe, size window, leading-edge genes per significant set, the unmapped/duplicate-symbol share, and a reproducibility record.

Limits worth stating up front: 12,000 genes is a reduced feature space (not a full transcriptome), so the effective universe for every set is smaller than the collection assumes and set sizes must be reported after intersection. Six vs six unpaired samples is adequate for a set-level test but modest; hallmark results are hypotheses for follow-up, not established mechanism, and enrichment results are known to differ between methods.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top-500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic with MSigDB Hallmark
Enrichment report with leading edge, collection versions, reproducibility record

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. State the size of the significant list in the report.
